meta.title: Overflow
meta.description: What happens to the items a crowded hour cannot place: the "More" chip, the dialog behind it, and the table you can shape.

basics.intro: The timeline places items in columns, up to maxColumns of them. When an hour holds more than fit, the rest are collected into a group, and the group becomes a More chip on the grid. Opening the chip opens a dialog with the whole group in a table.
points: A group covers consecutive hours only while it stays inside overflowMergeWindow — see Timeline view.
The chip’s accessible name says how many items it holds and from what time.
A chip is also a pin sentinel: the pinnable items inside it pin when the chip scrolls past.
The dialog is a native modal, so the browser contains focus, <kbd>Escape</kbd> closes it, and the backdrop is a click target.

columns.intro: By default the table shows the time, the level, the title, the description and an action that opens the item’s detail. overflowColumns replaces that set with your own:
columns.sorting: A column sorts when it has a sortValue; one without is inert. Clicking a sortable header sorts ascending, clicking it again reverses, and changing the column returns to the first page. Ties break by compareItems, in the direction being sorted. Sort and page are controlled or uncontrolled like everything else, and reset each time the dialog opens unless you hold them.

points: The dialog is labelled by its title, which carries the number of items in the group.
The table is a real table: column headers carry aria-sort, and a sortable header is a button inside the header cell.
Opening an item from a row stacks a second dialog over the first; closing it returns focus to the row’s action.
Paging keeps focus in the pagination, and the page list is the same one the visible numbers show.
renderMoreLabel replaces the text on the chip; the moreChip, overflowDialog, overflowTable and pagination parts replace the markup.
localization.overflow holds the title, the column headers and the close labels.
The dialog and the table live in a chunk of their own, loaded the first time a chip is opened.
Overflow is a timeline idea; the list shows every item and never collapses any of them.
The table shows one group at a time — the one whose chip was opened.
Columns are not resizable by the reader, and their widths are the ones your column definitions ask for.
